messages.content: This is Liveline, a real-time animated line chart control for Uno Platform, shown on a live random-walk feed.

Liveline is one Uno single project, `Liveline.Demo/Liveline.Demo.csproj` (Uno.Sdk from `global.json`, heads net10.0-desktop and net10.0-browserwasm, UnoFeatures Material, Toolkit, Skia, SkiaRenderer). The chart control lives in the project's `Liveline/` folder; the page is the demo.

Key files:
- `MainPage.xaml`: a single `liveline:LivelineChart` named `Chart` inside a rounded `Border` with a `ThemeShadow`, at most 720 wide and 360 high, centred, inside a Toolkit `SafeArea` grid.
- `MainPage.xaml.cs`: the feed. It sets `Chart.Theme` (`#4CAF50`, dark) and `IsLoading`, waits 3 s on a `DispatcherTimer`, seeds 60 points, then adds a random-walk value every 150 ms (with an 8% chance of a spike), keeps the last 60 points, and sets `Chart.Data` and `Chart.Value`.
- `Liveline/LivelineChart.cs`: the public `UserControl`. Dependency properties: `Data`, `Value`, `Theme`, `ShowGrid`, `ShowBadge`, `ShowFill`, `ShowTrackingLine`, `Momentum`, `LerpSpeed`, `IsLoading`, `IsPaused`, `WindowStart`/`WindowEnd`/`NowTime`, `Forecast`/`ForecastOpacity`, brush overrides (`ChartBackground`, `LineBrush`, `FillTopBrush`, `FillBottomBrush`, `GridLineBrush`, `LabelBrush`, `BadgeTextBrush`, `LabelHaloBrush`), `StrokeThickness`, `PlotPadding`, `ValueMin`/`ValueMax`, `Typeface` and `Markers`. Every property change pushes one immutable state to the canvas.
- `Liveline/LivelineChartCanvas.cs`: an `SKCanvasElement` that draws the frame with the renderers in `Liveline/Rendering/` (grid, line and fill, badge, markers, and the live dot that `Momentum` turns on) over a `RenderContext`.
- `Liveline/Animation/LerpEngine.cs`: per-frame easing (by `LerpSpeed`) of the line, the value range and the badge toward their targets.
- `Liveline/Models/`: `LivelinePoint` (time, value), `LivelineTheme` (one colour plus dark or light; `Helpers/ColorHelper.cs` derives the palette), `LivelineMarker`, `MomentumDirection`.

Animation: the control subscribes to `CompositionTarget.Rendering` while the line is moving and unsubscribes as soon as `TickAnimation()` reports it has settled; the next property change re-attaches. Keep that: a held Rendering subscription makes the compositor draw at display refresh for nothing. Allocate paints and paths outside the per-frame path.

The page uses code-behind on purpose: the feed is a timer, and there is no navigation, MVUX or MVVM. Data is simulated; nothing leaves the device.

Build: `dotnet build Liveline.Demo/Liveline.Demo.csproj -f net10.0-desktop`, or `-f net10.0-browserwasm` for WebAssembly. There are no tests.

The app is built and running. The user may ask me to modify it.
